Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

A method and system are provided for automatically portioning workpieces, such as food products, by simulating portioning the workpieces in accordance with the one or more desired shapes of the final piece(s) as a directly controlled physical characteristic (parameter/specification) as well as one or more resulting indirectly controlled physical characteristics (parameters/specifications). The desired shape(s) of the final piece(s) are defined by a plurality of manipulatable reference coordinates. A workpiece is scanned to obtain scanning information, then portioning of the workpiece is simulated in accordance with the desired shape(s) of the final piece(s) defined by the directly controlled reference coordinates, thereby to determine the one or more indirectly controlled physical characteristics of the one or more final pieces to be portioned from the workpiece. The simulated portioning of the workpiece is performed for multiple combinations of directly controlled shapes as defined by the modified or edited reference coordinates and indirectly controlled physical characteristics until an acceptable set of a directly controlled shape and resulting one or more indirectly controlled physical characteristics is determined.

outputs.L1: A method and system are provided for automatically portioning workpieces, such as food products, by simulating the portioning of the workpieces in accordance with one or more desired shapes of the final piece(s), where such shape(s) serve as directly controlled physical characteristics, parameters, or specifications, together with one or more resulting indirectly controlled physical characteristics, parameters, or specifications. The desired shape(s) of the final piece(s) are defined by a plurality of manipulatable reference coordinates. A workpiece is scanned to obtain scanning information, after which portioning of the workpiece is simulated in accordance with the desired shape(s) of the final piece(s), as defined by the directly controlled reference coordinates, to determine the one or more indirectly controlled physical characteristics of the one or more final pieces to be portioned from the workpiece. The simulated portioning of the workpiece is performed for multiple combinations of directly controlled shapes, as defined by modified or edited reference coordinates, and indirectly controlled physical characteristics until an acceptable set comprising a directly controlled shape and the resulting one or more indirectly controlled physical characteristics is determined.

A technique and associated system are disclosed for automatically dividing workpieces, including food items, into portions. The process models how the workpiece would be portioned based on one or more target shapes for the finished piece or pieces, where the target shape is treated as a directly managed physical parameter, along with one or more physical properties that result indirectly from that choice. The intended final shape or shapes are specified using multiple adjustable reference coordinates.

The workpiece is scanned to collect scan data, after which the portioning operation is simulated according to the desired final shape or shapes established by the directly controlled reference coordinates. This simulation is used to identify one or more indirectly controlled physical characteristics of the final piece or pieces that would be cut from the workpiece. The simulated portioning is repeated for various combinations of directly controlled shapes, as represented by altered or revised reference coordinates, and the resulting indirectly controlled physical characteristics, until a satisfactory combination of a directly controlled shape and its corresponding indirectly controlled characteristic or characteristics is found.
outputs.L3:
The method provides an automated way to portion workpieces, such as food products, by simulating cutting operations before the actual cuts are made. Instead of relying only on fixed cutting patterns or manual judgment, the system uses a model of the workpiece and predicts how different cutting strategies will affect the final portions.

A desired final shape for each portion is defined and controlled through a set of reference coordinates. These reference coordinates can be adjusted or manipulated to change the intended geometry of the final pieces. By editing the coordinates, the user or system can directly influence the target shape of the portions to be produced.

Before portioning begins, the workpiece is scanned to collect information about its size, shape, volume, density, surface profile, or other relevant properties. This scan data is used to create a representation of the workpiece that can be used in a simulation of the portioning process.

The simulation then applies virtual cuts to the scanned workpiece according to the selected reference coordinates and desired final shapes. From this simulation, the system determines physical characteristics of the resulting portions that are not directly controlled by the reference coordinates. These indirectly controlled characteristics may include weight, volume, thickness, yield, trim loss, or other quality-related parameters.

Different combinations of edited reference coordinates and their resulting portion characteristics are simulated and evaluated. The process may be repeated many times, with the reference coordinates being adjusted between simulations, until the predicted outcome satisfies the relevant requirements. Once an acceptable portioning result is identified, the corresponding cutting strategy can be used to portion the actual workpiece.
outputs.L4:
The method concerns the automated portioning of workpieces, particularly irregular natural products such as fish, meat, poultry, or other food items, into portions having desired final characteristics. In such products, the size, weight, thickness, outline, and internal structure may vary considerably from one workpiece to another. Because of this variation, it is difficult to obtain portions that consistently meet commercial requirements if the cutting operation is based only on fixed cutting patterns or on a single measured parameter such as weight.

In the described method, each workpiece is first scanned or otherwise measured to obtain information about its geometry and, where relevant, its internal or external properties. The scanning may determine, for example, the length, width, thickness profile, contour, volume distribution, density, defects, bones, fat lines, or other features of the workpiece. From this measured information, a data representation of the workpiece is generated. This representation can then be used by a control system to simulate possible cuts before any physical cutting is carried out.

The desired final portions are defined by shapes. These shapes are not merely fixed templates, but are associated with reference coordinates that can be manipulated. A reference coordinate may define, for example, the position, orientation, scale, or deformation of a desired shape relative to the workpiece. By moving or adjusting these reference coordinates, the system can test different ways of fitting one or more desired portion shapes into the scanned workpiece. In this way, the required final shape of a portion can be directly controlled, while still allowing the system flexibility in how the shape is placed or adapted to the particular workpiece being processed.

For each possible arrangement, the system simulates a corresponding portioning plan. A portioning plan may include one or more cut lines, cutting surfaces, blade paths, water-jet paths, saw paths, or other dividing operations needed to produce the selected portions. The simulation allows the system to predict the result of the cutting operation without actually cutting the workpiece. The predicted portions can then be evaluated against a set of requirements.

Some requirements are directly controlled by the selected shape and the manipulated reference coordinates. These may include the outline of the portion, the intended contour, the relative position of a cut, the orientation of the portion, or the relationship between adjacent portions. Other characteristics are indirectly controlled. These may include weight, volume, thickness, yield, surface area, fat content, bone content, or other physical properties that result from the selected shape and cut placement. Although these indirectly controlled characteristics are not necessarily specified as the primary shape definition, they can be calculated or estimated from the scanned data and the simulated cuts.

The system tests multiple combinations of desired shapes and reference-coordinate settings. For example, it may shift a shape along the length of the workpiece, rotate it, scale it, mirror it, stretch it, or otherwise adapt its position and configuration. For each tested combination, the system determines whether the resulting portions satisfy the directly controlled shape requirements. It also evaluates whether the indirectly controlled physical characteristics fall within acceptable limits, such as a target weight range, minimum thickness, maximum trim loss, or required yield.

If a tested combination does not meet the required criteria, the system rejects that simulated portioning plan and tests another combination. This process may continue until an acceptable plan is found. In some implementations, the system may search through a large number of possible combinations and select the best one according to a ranking or optimization function. The selected plan may be the first plan that satisfies all mandatory requirements, or it may be the plan that provides the best overall result when several acceptable plans are available.

Once an acceptable portioning plan has been identified, the system can control a cutting apparatus to portion the workpiece according to that plan. The cutting apparatus may include knives, circular blades, bandsaws, water jets, lasers, or other cutting tools. The control system uses the simulated cut information to guide the cutting device so that the physical cuts correspond to the selected plan.

The advantage of this approach is that it combines shape-based control with prediction of physical product characteristics. Instead of attempting to control only weight or relying on fixed cutting patterns, the method allows desired product shapes to be defined and adjusted through reference coordinates. At the same time, the system can ensure that the portions produced from those shapes have suitable properties such as weight, volume, thickness, and yield. This makes the method especially useful for processing natural workpieces whose geometry varies from item to item, while still producing portions that meet predetermined commercial or quality requirements.

**The**

“The” is one of the smallest words in the English language, yet it carries great importance. It helps us point to something specific, something known, or something already mentioned. We say *the sun* because there is only one sun in our sky. We say *the book* when both speaker and listener understand which book is being discussed.

Although “the” may seem simple, it gives clarity and direction to a sentence. Without it, language can sound vague or incomplete. For example, “I saw dog” feels unfinished, but “I saw the dog” tells us that the speaker is referring to a particular dog.

“The” is also one of the most common words in English. It appears everywhere: in stories, conversations, articles, songs, and speeches. Its quiet presence helps connect ideas and guide meaning. Even though it is short, “the” plays a powerful role in communication.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent-style abstract for an automated food portioning system that scans a workpiece, uses adjustable reference coordinates to define desired final shapes, simulates cuts, and evaluates resulting indirect characteristics until acceptable portions are found.
counterfactuals.output: An automated food portioning system includes a scanning device configured to obtain dimensional data of a food workpiece, a controller configured to establish adjustable reference coordinates corresponding to desired final portion shapes, and a cutting simulation module configured to generate prospective cut patterns based on the dimensional data and the reference coordinates. The controller evaluates simulated portions according to indirect characteristics derived from the simulated cuts, including at least one of predicted weight, volume, yield, shape conformity, thickness distribution, or defect inclusion. The reference coordinates and cut patterns are iteratively adjusted until one or more simulated portions satisfy predetermined acceptance criteria. A cutting apparatus may then be controlled to cut the workpiece according to the accepted cut pattern, thereby producing food portions having desired final characteristics while improving yield and consistency.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a concise invention summary describing a method and system for automatically portioning workpieces by directly controlling final piece shape and indirectly determining characteristics such as size, weight, or yield through simulated portioning.
counterfactuals.output: A method and system for automatically portioning workpieces, such as food products, by controlling the final geometric shape of each portion rather than directly targeting weight or yield. The system acquires dimensional data for a workpiece, generates a digital model, and simulates one or more portioning patterns to predict resulting characteristics such as portion size, weight, volume, trim, and yield. Based on the simulation, the system selects or adjusts a cutting plan that produces portions having desired final shapes while indirectly satisfying target production criteria. A controller then directs cutting equipment, such as blades, waterjets, or other portioning devices, to execute the selected plan. This enables consistent shape-based portioning while optimizing secondary attributes without requiring direct control of those attributes during cutting.

The target shapes are manipulated relative to the scanned item, including by translation, rotation, scaling, deformation, or other parameter adjustment. Multiple candidate cutting outcomes are simulated based on different shape positions and cutting parameters, and each simulated outcome is evaluated against one or more criteria, such as weight, volume, yield, dimensional tolerance, trim, fat content, or product grade. counterfactuals.prompt: Create an abstract for a computer-controlled portioning apparatus that scans food workpieces and iteratively simulates different coordinate-defined final shapes to satisfy both directly controlled shape parameters and resulting indirectly controlled physical characteristics.
counterfactuals.output: A computer-controlled portioning apparatus and method are provided for cutting food workpieces into portions having selected final configurations and physical characteristics. The apparatus scans each workpiece to obtain dimensional data and generates a digital representation of the workpiece. A control system iteratively simulates a plurality of candidate final portion shapes defined by coordinate data relative to the scanned workpiece. For each candidate shape, the control system evaluates directly controlled shape parameters, such as length, width, thickness, perimeter, area, or contour, and estimates indirectly controlled physical characteristics resulting from the candidate shape, such as weight, volume, yield, thickness distribution, cook performance, or appearance. The control system selects a final shape satisfying one or more prescribed shape constraints and one or more target physical characteristic criteria, and controls a cutting device to portion the workpiece according to the selected coordinate-defined shape. The simulation and selection process may be repeated for successive portions or workpieces to optimize compliance with product specifications, reduce waste, and improve portion uniformity.
